cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to Timothy, the man he calls his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2). He's just told Timothy to fight the good fight (1 Timothy 1:18), and now he says 'First of all, then,' so you KNOW this is the top of the list. He urges that petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgiving be offered.

cards.question: Paul wants petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgiving offered. Who are they for?
Then Paul names one group in particular for that prayer list. Which group is it?

answers.text: Kings and all those in authority

cards.question: Paul says to pray for kings and those in authority so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.

cards.text: Tranquil and quiet? Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer next to dead batteries arguing all night over who had the most charge left, so I will TAKE it. Now Paul tells Timothy how this praying looks in the sight of God our Savior.

cards.question: How does Paul say this kind of praying for everyone looks in the sight of God our Savior?
Paul says God our Savior wants only certain people to be saved.

cards.text: God our Savior wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Everyone, friend, not just the people who actually reply in the group chat.
Then Paul gives the reason: there is one God. And between God and men, there is one mediator.

cards.question: Paul says there is one mediator between God and men. Who is it?

cards.text: And Christ Jesus doesn't just stand in the middle like a referee. He gives Himself.

cards.question: Paul says Christ Jesus gave Himself as a ___ for all.

cards.text: Paul calls this the testimony given at just the right time. For this reason, he says, he was appointed as a preacher, an apostle and a teacher.

cards.question: Paul says he was appointed as a faithful and true teacher of the ___.

cards.text: Then Paul adds, "I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything." Friend, I say that every time I tell a baker I only tasted ONE chocolate chip, and Paul's the one of us who actually means it.
Next Paul turns to the men everywhere. He wants them to pray, lifting up holy hands. BOTH hands, friend, not one up and the other one still scrolling the phone.

cards.question: Paul wants the men everywhere to pray with holy hands lifted up. What does he want that praying to be without?

cards.text: Then Paul turns to the women. He wants them to dress respectably, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes.

cards.question: Instead of braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes, what does Paul want the women adorned with?
Paul says good deeds are proper for women who profess to worship God.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness."

cards.question: Paul says there are two things he does not permit a woman to do. What are they?

answers.text: Teach or exercise authority over a man
Own land or run a business of her own
Travel or trade in the market alone

cards.text: She is to remain quiet, Paul says. Then he gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says ___ was formed first and then ___.
Paul says it was Adam who was deceived.

cards.text: Paul says it was not Adam who was deceived. It was the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.
Then Paul ends with a word for women. He says they will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love and holiness, and he adds one more thing to that list.

cards.question: Paul says women will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith and love and holiness with ___.

findings.problem: The question relies on "that prayer list" from an earlier card instead of restating the needed context, such as Paul's call to pray for everyone. It is not fully self-contained when the earlier card is no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the question about being tranquil and quiet, the junk-drawer joke, and the setup about God our Savior.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup only says that Christ Jesus gives Himself. It provides no basis for reasoning to "ransom" rather than "lesson" or "warning," so the blank asks for BSB wording the baker has not seen rather than a meaning supported by the earlier cards.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup names Paul as a preacher, apostle and teacher but gives no clue about whom he teaches. The baker cannot reason out "Gentiles" from the earlier cards, making this a guess at the line's wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: Paul turns to the men, he wants them to pray with holy hands, and the phone joke follows as a third sentence.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The only setup is that Paul gives a reason. Nothing in the earlier cards supplies the creation order or points to Adam and Eve, so both blanks depend on recalling or guessing wording rather than reasoning from the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: All three answers are plausible virtues, and saying only that Paul "adds one more thing" gives no reason to select self-control over gentleness or patience. Its earlier appearance in verse 9 does not establish that Paul repeats it here, so the choice still depends on wording recall or luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
